# Cannon School — International Travel — Deep Research

**⚠️ This is an AI-generated research summary, not a primary source.** The PDF was
produced by Claude deep research. Treat every claim below as a **lead to verify**, not as
evidence. A fact may reach the app only once it has been confirmed on a live page, normally
the school's own site, and that page's URL has been recorded in the companion
`Cannon School - International Travel - Source URLs.md`. A claim that cannot be confirmed
stays here as research history and renders nowhere.

Global Education Programs — Research Dossier (as of October 2026)"*, a 14-page
deep-research PDF (filename `Cannon School Concord NC_ Global Travel and Global Education
Programs Research Dossier 2026.pdf`) the user supplied while running `/global-exposure`.
It was written from the `/global-exposure` prompt template (v2), sections 1–20. Every URL
below is copied from the PDF; the Source URLs file records which were re-checked and what
they actually say.

Source-type tags are copied from the PDF: **[Official]** = cannonschool.org pages, news
posts and finalsite-hosted PDFs; **[Secondary]** = third-party.

**Student names.** The PDF names no student. The school's own pages name students and
trip leaders; the app names none of them.

**Costs and exact travel dates.** Recorded here per the data-provenance standard. They are
**not rendered** on the page (privacy rule).

**Planning notes on the PDF's accuracy** (found at verification, 2026-10-15):
- **The Global Studies Mastery Credits PDF loads.** The PDF says it "could not be
 retrieved (tool restriction, tried twice)". A plain `curl` of the resource-manager URL
 redirects to `CANNONSCHOOLGLOBALSTUDIESMASTERYCREDITSupdatedAugust2021.pdf` and returns
 its full text: four strands, CS1–CS4. "Could not load" was a tool failure, not a finding
 — the same lesson as Country Day's Middle School page.
- **The TECHO Dominican Republic article loads, and it is the richest trip record.** The
 PDF lists it as "article body not retrieved" and fills its details from TECHO USA's
 site. The school's own article gives 22 Upper School students, six days in Santo
 Domingo, selection by interview, and states the Winterm 2025 Costa Rica TECHO trip
 itself — so that trip no longer needs the Secondary source.
- **The Wayback Machine is reachable.** The PDF says it was not. CDX lists 21 Winterm-page
 snapshots (2019–2026) and 14 International Programs snapshots (2021–2025). The Winterm
 gallery shows the same two trips (Costa Rica Sámara; Sea Island Habitat) from Dec 2022
 through Oct 2025. A 2019 snapshot links a now-gone `/academics/international-programs/travel-abroad`
 page announcing a Lower School family trip to Greece for summer 2020 — absent from the PDF.
- **The Hamburg Open trip is a Cannon Studios (event-technology) trip**, not a global-
 education one. Verified, but marginal for this area.
- **The Tianli (Luzhou, China) sister-school exchange** appears on no cannonschool.org
 page. Secondary only; not renderable.

Cannon School has a real global-education program, but it is small and mostly in the Upper
School. The program is called "International Programs." It includes a senior-year "Global
Studies Certificate," a teacher "Global Education Badge" and a mix of trips: Winterm trips,
summer trips and service builds. The school does not publish trip prices, a current trip
list, a selection process, safety rules or any participation numbers. It is not in Round
Square. The only travel-specific money is a named endowment whose terms are not shown. If
global travel matters to you, ask the school about it directly. The website will not answer
most of your questions.

sections.text:
- **What exists:** an "International Programs" office page with a mission statement; a
 senior "Global Studies Certificate" awarded at Senior Night; a required senior course,
 "Honors Glocal Perspectives"; Winterm "Trips and Certifications," open to grades 9–11;
 recent student trips to China (summer 2025), Costa Rica (Middle School, summer 2026) and
 the Dominican Republic (TECHO service build, Winterm January 2026); and a faculty Global
 Education Badge with 21 recipients from 2017 to 2024 (our tally).
 https://www.cannonschool.org/academics/international-programs ;
 https://www.cannonschool.org/academics/upper-school/winterm [Official]
- **What's missing:** no trip costs or deposits, no current or upcoming trip list, no
 selection or application process, no travel vendor, no safety, insurance or passport
 guidance, no count of how many students travel or earn the certificate, and no Round
 Square or similar network membership. The rules that replaced the original certificate
 requirements ("Global Studies Mastery Credits," from the Class of 2024 on) sit in a PDF
 the researchers could not open. *(Planning note: it opens — see above.)*
- **Earliest grade for international travel:** never stated. The youngest travelers on
 record are Middle School students on a summer 2026 Costa Rica trip (grades not given).
 Winterm trips are "open to students from 9th through 11th grade."
- **The money:** need-based aid covers "Required overnight class trips" but does not list
 optional international trips (https://www.cannonschool.org/admission/financial-aid).
 Four "Special Funds" are listed, including the "John Riley Endowment for Science, Service,
 and Travel" and the "Equity of Experience Endowment." "Each fund has unique eligibility
 criteria…". A named fund's payout supports "the purpose of the fund as defined by the
 donor," per "a written endowment agreement"
 (https://www.cannonschool.org/support-cannon/endowment). Criteria and amounts not
 published.
- **Faculty travel is better documented than student travel.** In 2026, donor-funded
 awards (the inaugural Helfrich Catalyst Fellowship and a Kimbrough award) sent teachers
 to Peru and Finland
 (https://www.cannonschool.org/news-and-stories/in-the-news-details/~board/cannon-news-cougar-news-internal-sources/post/cannon-educators-earndonor-funded-awardsto-bring-global-perspectives-back-to-the-classroom).

sections.text:
- **Official name:** page titled "International Programs." Mission (singular): "The mission
 of the International Program at Cannon School is to promote global competency by
 broadening the experiences of students through travel, summer exchange, study, and
 service; to provide an avenue for thinking globally and acting locally; to develop a
 culture that encourages individual summer exchange and group travel." [Official]
 https://www.cannonschool.org/academics/international-programs
- **Stated purposes of trips and exchanges:** "Develop global competency; Cultural
 exchange; Practice a foreign language; Student exchange immersion; Historical
 perspectives; Scientific inquiry; Personal growth; Service opportunity; Earn the Global
 Studies Certificate; Global Studies competitions." [Official] same URL.
- **Framework:** a "Cultural Competencies Framework" graphic (text not extractable). The
 school's overall academic framework is "Adaptive Expertise," and the summer 2026 Costa
 Rica story ties the trip to "adaptive expertise." [Official] https://www.cannonschool.org/ ;
 …/post/learning-beyond-the-classroom-in-costa-rica
- **Who runs it:** no office or director title. The page lists "Jady Arriaga-Arango, Upper
 School information contact for Global Studies." A Faculty Friday profile: "Upper School
 Spanish teacher and world languages department chair," "joined Cannon in 2018," "Before
 Cannon... served as a U.S. Global Education Coordinator." [Official]
 https://www.cannonschool.org/news-and-stories/in-the-news-details/~board/faculty-fridays/post/meet-jady-arriaga
- **How it is organized:** Upper School-centered — certificate, senior Glocal Perspectives
 course, Winterm trips and outside events (World Affairs Council of Charlotte, World Quest,
 Model UN). MS and LS global learning comes through the language program, social studies
 units and occasional trips. No JrK–12 structure published.
- **Start date:** NOT PUBLISHED. International Programs page created "2020-06-08", last
 published "2025-09-10" (page metadata). First teacher badges "2017." Secondary sources
 date the China sister-school exchange to 2004 (§4).

- **Name:** "Cannon School Global Studies Certificate"; the page also says "US Global
 Studies Certificate." The course catalog and the 2025–26 profile say "Global Education
 Certificate." **Naming conflict flagged.** [Official] international-programs ;
 https://resources.finalsite.net/images/v1738691920/cannonschoolorg/uttbrksgq9kxdyjdrjpr/CannonAcademicCourseCatalog2025-26DIGITAL1.pdf (p. 38)
- **Purpose:** "designed to recognize students who demonstrate a global mindset and embody
 the qualities of a global citizen... The certificate is awarded during Senior Night."
- **Requirements (original version):**
 1. "Students have completed World History I and II, World Language I and II and III."
 2. "During their Senior year, students have enrolled in the Glocal Perspectives Class,
 which includes completing a Capstone Essay and delivering a presentation on a global
 topic of their choice."
 3. "AT LEAST two" of: "International Exposure: Participate in a Cannon School-sponsored
 spring or summer international educational trip, live in a foreign country for at
 least one month, or host an international student"; "Winterm Courses: Complete a
 second Winterm course, such as an international trip, service learning within local
 international communities, or a global issues course offered by any department";
 "Global Education Events: Attend two approved global education events, such as the
 World Affairs Council of Charlotte, World Quest, SDLC, Chapel Hill, and Lenoir-Rhyne
 Foreign Language Competition, or participate in Model UN, among others."
- **Current version:** "Starting with the Class of 2024, please refer to the Global Studies
 Mastery Credits requirements." Linked PDF
 (https://www.cannonschool.org/fs/resource-manager/view/3bd2ca09-c697-4ae8-ac6c-4ff7cbe2836d)
 "could not be retrieved." *(Planning note: it loads — content in the Source URLs file.)*
- **Required course:** "HONORS GLOCAL PERSPECTIVES — Prerequisite: Open to seniors only.
 This course does not fulfill the World Language requirement. This course is required for
 completion of the Global Education Certificate." Uses "a service learning model";
 culminates in "Capstone projects focused on a chosen glocal issue." [Official] catalog p. 38.
- **Language courses that count:** catalog marks Spanish III–V, AP Spanish, French III–V,
 AP French, Chinese III–V and AP Chinese as counting toward the certificate (pp. 33–37).
- **Year started, graduate counts, associated award:** NOT PUBLISHED.
- **Teacher counterpart:** "Teachers can earn the Global Education Badge by completing at
 least 100 hours of professional development in global studies/education and submitting a
 Capstone project focused on a global issue." [Official]
